readme.html:
Design with an elephant. Review with a goldfish.

Install  ·  Quickstart  ·  Documentation  ·  Website


Thousands of Google engineers use EGM, an open-source plugin, to draft specs with deep-context agents and stress-test them with zero-context subagents before writing code.

Elephant holds your project context and drafts the specification. Goldfish reviewers examine the draft and referenced source material without the earlier conversation, helping expose unstated assumptions and blind spots. You make the architectural trade-offs and approve the specification before implementing.

Use it when a feature needs design decisions before implementation. For a small, clear bug fix, use your normal coding workflow.

Install

Choose your coding agent. Install the complete plugin so its skills can read the reviewer prompts and document standards.

Antigravity

agy plugin install https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model

Claude Code

claude plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
claude plugin install egm@egm

Codex

codex plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
codex plugin add egm@egm

Start a new session after installation. For Claude Cowork and ChatGPT Work, see the setup guide.

Try your first design

Open your project in your coding agent and choose a feature that needs design decisions. This example adds webhook delivery: what should happen when a delivery fails, or the same event arrives twice?

The commands below are shown without a prefix. In Antigravity (agy CLI) and Claude Code, add the /egm: prefix, for example /egm:egm-brainstorm. In Codex, select the corresponding EGM skill from the skill picker. Brainstorming and review require a session that can create fresh subagents.

Explore the idea

/egm-brainstorm Add webhook delivery to this project.

Discuss requirements and trade-offs with the agent. Fresh reviewers challenge the proposal, and the agent saves the agreed direction in concepts_brief.md.

Draft the specification

/egm-draft

The agent turns the brief into design_draft.md, pausing after each section for your feedback in chat.

Review the draft

/egm-review design_draft.md

Use the draft path returned by the agent.

Fresh reviewers check the design, its clarity, its fit with the code, and its implementation plan. Choose which findings to address. When you approve the design, ask your coding agent to implement it.

See the workflow guide for the full process, including saving approved specifications under docs/designs/.

How it works

RoleContextResponsibility
ElephantYour project, requirements, and earlier decisionsExplore the problem and draft the specification.
GoldfishThe document and its referenced source material, without the earlier conversationFind missing assumptions, unclear requirements, and implementation risks.
YouThe goals and constraints that matterResolve trade-offs, approve the design, and decide what to build.

Goldfish reviews require fresh subagent contexts. If your agent cannot create them, EGM stops the review. A review does not replace tests or human judgment. See supported environments and verification limits.

Choose a skill

You can use each skill when you need it. You do not have to follow the full sequence.

SkillUse it to…
 BrainstormTest an idea and write a concept brief.
 DraftTurn a brief or existing notes into a design document.
 ResolveWork through review findings and agree on changes.
 BootstrapCreate or update documentation for an existing codebase.
 ReviewReview a design with fresh agents across five stages.
 Review loopRun a configured group of reviewers for a specific review task.
 Drift reportCompare checked-in documents with the current source code.

Learn more

  • Getting started: the workflow and project layout.
  • Setup: installation, agent capabilities, and known limits.
  • Architecture: how skills and reviewers fit together.
  • Testing: checks, execution records, and verification limits.
  • Dave Rensin’s original essay: the ideas behind EGM.

Contribute

Read contributing for PRs, issues for bugs, and discussions for questions.

License

Apache 2.0. This is not an officially supported Google product.

skills.name: egm-bootstrap
skills.description: Bootstrap directory README.md files across a repository subtree.

skills.name: egm-brainstorm
skills.description: - Interactive ideation and brainstorming skill for the Elephant & Goldfish Model (EGM). Helps turn half-baked concepts into structured hypotheses via clarifying questions, review, and iterative refinement. Produces an RFC summary for human review or more detailed design with /egm-draft.

skills.name: egm-draft
skills.description: - Drafts a design document section-by-section using the concepts brief from egm-brainstorm (or user notes). This is the second step in the Elephant-Goldfish (EGM) feature flow. Use when you are ready to write a design doc after aligning on requirements + solution.

skills.name: egm-drift-report
skills.description: - Runs drift detection on all design documents to check for document and code consistency. Produces an actionable report with differences. Use when the user asks to detect drift or check for consistency across all design documents or READMEs in a directory.

skills.name: egm-resolve
skills.description: - The Elephant resolution skill. Ingests flat deficiency reports from concurrent Goldfish reviewers, applies automated fixes for PROPOSE FIX items via UI multiple-choice gates, and presents interactive negotiation/re-sync checkpoints.

skills.name: egm-review-loop
skills.description: - Executes the Antagonistic-Review process from the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) via an automated multi-agent review loop to audit documents against qualitative standards and structural templates, and automatically apply approved fixes. Use when reviewing design docs, READMEs, feature specification

skills.name: egm-review
skills.description: - Orchestrates the EGM Goldfish Review Protocol. Used as part of the EGM process to perform design document reviews. Executes five review phases: Initial Zoom Out Review, Comprehension Review, Design Critique, Intermediate Zoom Out Review, and Implementation Readiness.
